speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; can you describe exactly when these symptoms started and how severe the pain is on a scale of 1 to 10?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Spontaneous Esophageal Rupture)

The history of forceful vomiting, retching, followed by sudden chest pain and choking is highly suggestive of an esophageal rupture, likely complicated by the patient's recent alcohol consumption. I will need to confirm this suspicion immediately. REQUEST TEST: Serum Amylase and Lipase; REQUEST IMAGES: Chest X-Ray Upright and Lateral Decubitus.
